Monday, October 18, 2021  7:00 PM  Teleconference

In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and the continuing state of emergency, including masking and
social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via
teleconference. There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public may participate in
the meeting in the following ways:

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
Meeting ID: 845 7105 0920, Meeting Password: 869500. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using
the call-in option from a phone line.)

- Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be
an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s
SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments
can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 845 7105 0920, Meeting Password: 869500.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING
  OCTOBER 18, 2021

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 7:03 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
  Order N-29-20.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Romanelli,
  and Ciarolla (joined at 7:09 pm)

  Commissioners Absent:  Retz

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT
  MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 20, 2021

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted she asked about the design of the blue area
  which led to the talk about increasing the corkboard size and asked that the
  section be revised accordingly.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  PERISCHINA to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  SEPTEMBER 20, 2021, WITH REVISION.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEF (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a review of the event reporting
  that the event was a success with positive feedback from the community. She
  stated that the Equestrian Committee suggested a country western band with
  dancing. She further reported that the Rockwall, petting zoo, and pony rides were
  popular this year, with the pony rides being the most popular. Dignitaries this year
  included Supervisor Hahn, Rolling Hills Mayor Ms. Dieringer, Palos Verdes Board
  of Education President Mr. Brock, and Palos Verdes Library Board of Trustees
  President Kingston Wong. She suggested that the volleyball game and flag
  ceremony may be moved on the schedule to allow for earlier use of the arena for

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 18, 2021
   more parking. The canopy in the lunch area was very popular, which allowed for
  record sales for the Empty Saddle Club.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted the busy lines and difficulty people had
  buying tickets online due to connectivity issues.

  CHAIR POPE suggested a Wi-Fi hot spot or Square type device to swipe credit
  cards. She explained that some people claimed to not have received their
  postcards in the mail. She stated that parking was an issue during the event with
  parking extending out to Rolling Hills Rd. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith
  noted reaching out to the nearby community on Empty Saddle Road in the future to
  allow for parking on the way into the Empty Saddle Club. CHAIR POPE noted the
  popularity of the rock-climbing wall and green space area.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted many people were grateful for the event. She
  suggested Swipe to store card data without using Wi-Fi. She wanted to know the
  number of attendees per activity to better assess the need for future events.
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas detailed the tickets received for each
  event. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the margin of error caused by
  wristbands. COMMISSIONER BAIN added that the food lined was backed-up and
  wondered if there were opportunities to improve in the future. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA suggested that adding more staff in the kitchen to serve the crowd
  during peak times would be helpful. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA stated Sean
  Martin oversaw the food this year and that the food ran out twice because there
  was a larger turnout than expected.

  CHAIR POPE noted more volunteers are needed to stay with the Pepper Tree
  Foundation booth. The Commissioners agreed.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggested advertising the payment method for
  future events to ease onsite issues. COMMISSIONER BAIN added that advertising
  the ticket prices before customers get to the front of the line would help transactions
  go smoother and requested that more petty cash be available next year. CHAIR
  POPE suggested pre-selling tickets for easy pick up at the booth.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested a wristband only event in the future, he
  also wanted to see a small snack being sold along with the lunches. ACM Davis
  noted a possible food truck be added as a snack option. She also reminded the
  Commission that the City won the volleyball match against the Sheriff’s Department.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the Mayor’s Speech could use a small stage area to
  call attention to the speakers and to consider pausing ticket sales during the speech
  which may help draw more attention to the remarks. He further suggested posting
  ticket pricing signage on the tent awning to help those waiting in line for tickets.

  B.  CHANDLER PARK AND PEPPERWOOD PARK PLAYGROUND DISCUSSION

  Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis provided a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA was open to Pepperwood Park rather than Chandler
  Park for a playground.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the playground was not well received by the
  Equestrian Community.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if the Commission would go back to
  community engagement if Pepperwood Park were considered.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the community’s desire for Chandler Park
  and the Equestrian community’s desire for a play structure at Pepperwood Park
  and that there may be an impasse.
PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 18, 2021
   COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted some compromises have been met such as
  deciding on smaller, noiseless structures for the park. He questioned the amount
  of community support for the project as not much turn out has been seen in past
  meetings.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN favors surveying the community as has been done for other
  playground projects and deferred to COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA on the type of
  low profile non-mechanical play equipment preferred.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted that horses do not like noises they cannot see
  and may spook as a result. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if those concerns rule
  out Pepperwood Park. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA responded that the round pen
  is not as concerning as the horse has room for turning out. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI does not see the difference between the two pens. COMMISSIONER
  CIAROLLA noted the traffic adjacent to the round pen would drown out any noise
  from the play area.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the parent community’s negative reaction
  to Pepperwood’s location due to it being near a busy intersection.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the area was more covered than Butcher
  Park but he agrees to conducting a survey that canvases more than the immediate
  neighborhood to reach out to equestrians who use the parks.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked how big of an area the survey can cover.
  ACM Davis noted placing a QR code at the parks can lead attendees to the survey
  also using NextDoor posts, the equestrian community and schools will help gather
  various interested parties. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted the riders of
  Chandler Park typically stable their horses at Peter Weber Equestrian Center and
  that they should be reached out to as well.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if images of the type of play equipment could be
  included in the survey.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggests moving forward with the project in a
  timely manner as it seems to be progressing slowly.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK agreed with including renderings in the survey.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN recommends natural looking play equipment.

  CHAIR POPE opened the floor to public comment.

  Community Member Palacios of Palos Verdes Drive North is concerned about
  Pepperwood Park and would like to participate in the survey. She expressed that
  Rancho Vista Elementary is a great option outside of school hours but is not viable
  in the long term. She noted horses do at times use Palos Verdes Drive North near
  Crenshaw Boulevard and expressed concern with a play area being too close to
  the intersection at Pepperwood Park. She explained that if children playing is too
  noisy at Chandler Park, it would be the same issue at Pepperwood Park for horses.
  She stated that though a few homes are adjacent to Chandler Park, the sun sets at
  dusk and park hours and school hours will make Chandler Park a place for kids
  aged 5 and under.

  Community Member Jim Marziani of Roanwood Drive shared that the trail alongside
  Palos Verdes Drive North is close to the proposed play area which is a concern and
  that putting a structure in the area will no longer make it an open natural space. He
  expressed those parents are seen there showing their children nature, such as
  rabbits in the area and it should not be taken away with a structure.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 18, 2021
   Community Member Jackie Alonso appreciated the staff report and noted the
  success of the City Celebration. She added that the 7 pm Commission Meeting
  time can be difficult for young families to attend as it is a bedtime for many younger
  children. She stated that she is aware of no horse incidents at the past City
  Celebration event which had amplified sounds and much noise from attendees.
  She also noted that Highridge and Ernie Howlett Parks, which have horse trails,
  have had no incidents between children and horse rider safety with the current
  activities. She stated that Highridge Park is located next to Ridgecrest Middle
  School and is still next to the park with a playground. Ms. Alonso stated that the
  age focused on the park proposal is on younger kids and the time used at the park
  is limited within that age group. She furthers that utilizing the public schools is not
  a welcoming experience. Ms. Alonso also stated that driving on Palos Verdes Drive
  North during after school hours has many kids on the walkway near the trail with no
  horse incidents. She expressed that Pepperwood Park is not viable due to drainage
  costs, safety, and road noise and that Chandler Park is ideal for low profile play
  equipment.

  Community Members Rich and Kristine Oldroyd of Ranchview stated non-
  equestrians like him are not in favor of play equipment. He stated that play
  equipment in Pepperwood Park would add to the green space but in Chandler Park,
  it would take away green space. He noted that horses can spook easily and may
  injure riders. Mrs. Oldroyd stated concerns related to ADA requirements which
  would need to be clarified as access to Chandler from the parking lot would be
  difficult. She suggested that more exact drawings be presented in the survey for
  better understanding. And further stated that ADA compliance may impact spacing
  between play equipment and expand its initial footprint, it is deceptive to survey
  people without knowing the impact. Mr. Oldroyd concluded that this should not be
  framed as equestrians versus non-equestrians.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if any grants were available to aid ADA
  requirements. ACM Davis noted other ADA enhancement projects and that there
  is a City ADA budget annually.

  CHAIR POPE recommended a community survey as the next step in the process.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about cost boundaries for the project. ACM
  Davis noted more detailed cost boundaries would be for future discussion once
  there is a preliminary decision on interest and location.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA asked if ADA projects were planned for Chandler
  Park. ACM Davis noted there are ADA enhancements identified as part of an
  ongoing 20-year plan.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if getting approval from City Council could
  precede the survey to move things along and refine the survey. ACM Davis noted
  the opportunity to bring the project to the future policy development meeting
  typically held in March of each year.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted the process will be a long one as these
  types of projects take time.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK agrees to conduct a survey and to add renderings
  after more interest is shown from the initial survey to reduce costs.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI wants to provide City Council with a better proposal
  which includes a dollar figure for the project.

  CHAIR POPE noted Rockbluff Park’s survey was edited through email and if that
  could be done for this project. ACM Davis noted the survey was refined with the
  subcommittee and could be done with this
PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 18, 2021
   project’s subcommittee and brought to the Commission for ultimate City Council
  review.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted Rockbluff had a budget in the survey and that the
  City should not put out a survey with a budget that is not yet approved. She asked
  if there is a revision for Chandler Park’s ramp, why is the addition of the play area
  changing compliance with the ADA and that the City should comply with ADA
  requirements regardless. ACM Davis responded that the plan is already identified
  but if the project is planned, then the improvements must be completed at the same
  time.

  CHAIR POPE asked for staff to work with the Commission subcommittee members
  on the survey and return to the Commission before shared with City Council and
  ultimately the community.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggests having City Council buy-in to a ballpark
  figure for the project. ACM Davis noted that this could be done through an action
  item after the survey.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the City Council today may differ in the
  future when the project moves forward which may offer more funding.

  ACM Davis confirmed with the Commission that the survey is to address Chandler
  Park as the project site and will be drafted by the Commission members of
  subcommittee, return to the Commission approval and ultimately shared with the
  City Council before wide-spread community outreach.

  CHAIR POPE thanked the community members in attendance.

  C.  SNOW DAY

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the staff
  report.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if there were Pepper Tree Foundation funds for this
  event.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted the funds are available but would
  need to be approved by the City Council as a budget adjustment.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked what portion of the cost Waste Management could
  offset. ACM Davis noted they typically sponsor only part of the cost of the event.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if there were any events that generated
  funds to pay for the event. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the race brought
  in revenue for the Pepper Tree Foundation. ACM Davis noted the Foundation does
  have a balance.

  CHAIR POPE asked COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK if it was his idea. He replied
  that it would be a fun active family event and since Ernie Howlett Park has a natural
  bowl area that would accommodate the event well.  COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK stated that January is also a good time for the event and that perhaps
  coffee and cocoa could also be sold.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN agreed with COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK on a January
  date and to sell hot drinks to offset some cost. CHAIR POPE noted that the January
  date is ideal as well.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 18, 2021
   COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked how early these companies should be
  booked. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that six months is
  ideal but it depends on company availability.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted a Saturday morning event would be ideal
  and that February could also work while avoiding Superbowl Sunday.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggested looking to other cities that have done
  these types of snow days for guidance but agrees with having the event.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas asked the Commission if taking the
  $5,000 budget to City Council and if an after-school event is possible if a Saturday
  morning is not available.

  CHAIR POPE and COMMISSIONER BAIN and MCCORMICK noted that daylight
  would end too soon and that a Sunday morning is preferred as an alternative date.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE A SNOW DAY AT
  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK ON SATURDAY MORNING OF JANUARY 2022,
  ALTERNATIVELY FEBRUARY 2022, AT A BUDGET OF $5,000.

  AYES: Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Romanelli

  ABSENT: Retz

  The motion carries.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  D.  TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLE TOURNAMENT (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted that all entries this year are electronic,
  and a November date allows for a broader pool to advertise to as the school year is
  in session. Courts have been reserved and a food truck will be used this year in lieu
  of staff coordinating a food booth with volunteers. He explained that later matches
  will be held this year due to league matches in the mornings at the Jack Kramer Club.
  Sponsorship funds have arrived for a total of $4000 to date. He explained that staff
  hopes to have more up to date draw results this year.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about applicant numbers. Community
  Services Coordinator A-Haja noted only five registrations to date but more calls are
  coming in.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the registration numbers are equivalent to
  previous years. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja responded that the exact
  figures are not available but that numbers have risen in other local tennis tournaments
  in the area.

  E.  PARADE OF LIGHTS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted the parade agreement has been
  finalized by the City Attorney and will be taken to the Parade Director for signature.
  Volunteers are coming in and a subcommittee meeting will be taking place later this
  week to finalize a trophy area. Sponsorships are on track and local businesses will
  be contacted.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 18, 2021
   COMMISSIONER BAIN asked for the date of the event.  Community Services
  Coordinator A-Haja responded Saturday December 4th.

  ACM Davis noted the parade grand marshal is still being finalized but a hometown
  grand marshal has been identified as former Councilmember and Mayor, Judy
  Mitchell.

  COMMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if there was enough room for the displaced
  spectators in the mall and why the mall could not be used this year. ACM Davis
  responded that due to COVID the mall had some restrictions, however more
  bleachers and lighting will be used to place crowds throughout the wider route.

  CHAIR POPE LEFT THE COMMISSION MEETING AT 9:21 pm. VICE CHAIR
  CIAROLLA CHAIRED THE MEETING IN HER ABSENCE.

  F.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE REQUEST: PUBLIC RIDING RING RULES
  REVIEW - CHANDLER ARENA

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked how temporary the reprieve will be.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded six months but may be extended
  if approved by the Commission. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if any
  notifications need to be made to acknowledge the new rules. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that signs and a text alert will be made. ACM
  Davis also noted the City would notify the City’s list of trainers and the Palos Verdes
  Peninsula Horseman’s Association.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA asked if a motion is needed. ACM Davis noted an
  action item will be taken to City Council to approve the new guidelines.
  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if the months would be clarified. ACM Davis
  noted January through June could be used.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  CIAROLLA to:

  ACCEPT STAFF RECOMMENDATION BUT AMEND IT TO BE BROUGHT
  BACK IN JULY TO THE COMMISSION

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about a Halloween themed house
  decorating contest for next year.

  ACM Davis noted the Concert in the Park is scheduled this coming weekend and it
  will host games and a costume parade included as well.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN likes the idea of a costume parade and would suggest
  bringing that back if the event goes well. She asked if Halloween House decorating
  is popular in the City as she does not see many houses decorated.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted his neighborhood is decorated and would
  be willing participants.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if a Youth Sports Subcommittee meeting is
  on the horizon. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted a meeting will be
  planned for November and will include the
PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
OCTOBER 18, 2021
   Little League, Junior League, and Softball League’s interest in a contract with the
  City.

  B.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted a sign near the George F Canyon Learning
  Tree is damaged and a bench has been dismantled. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith noted the report and will inspect it tomorrow.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  None

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF SEPTEMBER 14, 2021

  Received and filed.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF SEPTEMBER 28, 2021

  Received and filed.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PETER WEBER CONTRACT RENEWAL

  ACM Davis noted staff is working with Peter Weber. The contract ends November

  B.  TENNIS COURT RENOVATION

  ACM Davis will bring the item to the Commission before City Council.

  C.  PICKLEBALL USAGE

  ACM Davis noted staff is trying to find ways to encourage use and will bring a report

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  VICE CHAIR CIAROLLA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 9:31 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED

  2021, AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH BE HELD VIA TELECONFERENCE.

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Lisa Van Ingen Pope
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
OCTOBER 18, 2021
